## Search & schema

### search_objects

*read-only* — Search CRM objects.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | string |  | Short user-facing description (<10 words), e.g. |
| `offset` | integer |  | Number of results to skip for pagination. |
| `paginationMode` | `"offset"` \\| `"cursor"` |  | Default "offset"; "cursor" for scans past 10,000 matches |
| `cursor` | object |  | nextCursor from the previous response (cursor mode only) |
| `cursorPageSize` | integer |  | Rows per cursor page (default 200, max 1000). |
| `queries` | object[] | yes | Array of search operations for different CRM object types |
| `timeframeStart` | string |  | Limit to objects after this date (bare YYYY-MM-DD = that full UTC day, or an ISO instant) |
| `timeframeEnd` | string |  | Limit to objects before this date (bare YYYY-MM-DD = through the end of that UTC day, or an ISO instant) |
| `timeframeField` | `"createdAt"` \\| `"updatedAt"` \\| `"storedAt"` \\| `"time"` \\| `"writtenAt"` |  | Timestamp field for timeframes (when omitted, defaults to "time" for native_emailmessage and updatedAt for everything else). |
| `propertiesToReturn` | string[] \\| string |  | Properties to return: omit for defaults, "*" for all, or an array of property IDs. |
| `includeRelationships` | boolean |  | Include related objects (default false), e.g. |

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Search CRM objects. Before first querying an object type in a conversation, call read_crm_schema for that type — it returns its properties, custom-property option IDs, relationships, and search recipes; skip it only for a trivial lookup by "email" (people) or by "name" (organizations) — a person-by-name lookup is NOT trivial, see KEY PATTERNS. Results are paginated (status partial|complete, with hasMore/nextOffset) and by default include only objectId, name/title, updatedAt, and a short description — pass propertiesToReturn "*" when fetching by objectIds.

WHERE: a condition is one flat object — property {"propertyId","operator","value"} or relationship {"relationship","targetObjectType","targetObjectId","operator"}. Combine with {"AND":[conditions or OR groups]} or {"OR":[conditions]}. For OR-of-AND logic use separate queries entries.

OPERATORS — text: contains, notContains, eq; email/phone add startsWith, endsWith; number/date: eq, neq, gt, gte ("on or after"), lt, lte ("on or before"); boolean: is; picklist: eq, neq, isAnyOf; multipicklist: containsAnyOf, containsAllOf; isNull/isNotNull take no value (and return no exact totals). Array operators take string arrays; all values are strings ("900" not 900). Picklist custom properties match by option ID (uuid), not label. Date-only values (YYYY-MM-DD) on date properties are day-semantic: eq matches any time that UTC day, lte includes the whole day, gt means strictly after it — eq "2026-07-31" is the right way to ask "on Jul 31".

RELATIONSHIP SEARCH: targetObjectId must come from a prior search ("meetings with Acme": search native_organization by name, then use its objectId with relationship "attendee"). Common edges: meetings/events "attendee"; opportunity→organization "subject"; opportunity→contact "related".

CALL SHAPE: a query entry holds ONLY objectType, objectIds, and where — propertiesToReturn, timeframes, and includeRelationships are top-level parameters applying to every query in the call (a key mistakenly placed inside a query entry is hoisted to the call level and applies to EVERY query). Every operator except isNull/isNotNull requires a non-empty value; to list ALL objects of a type, pass objectType with no where.

KEY PATTERNS (read_crm_schema has the full per-type recipes):
- native_contact has NO "name" property (and no "notes"): resolve a person by "firstName"/"lastName" contains (text-match — eq/neq on them ALWAYS fail) or by "email"; native_organization is the type with "name".
- Pipelines hold stages; stages hold opportunities. Opportunities have "stageId" NOT pipelineId: search the pipeline (includeRelationships true) → collect stage IDs → search opps by "stageId". Assume the sales pipeline unless told otherwise.
- Actions: "ownerEmail" eq for a person's tasks; AND-exclude status COMPLETED/DISMISSED/REDUNDANT (neq each) unless asked.
- native_meetingrecording = the record of meetings that actually happened (an object is created when the Day AI recorder attends a meeting): ALWAYS add timeframeStart and use the "attendee" relationship with a resolved objectId; NEVER use "attendees" or "domains" properties (calendar events only). Results carry "recordingStatus": only READY meetings have a transcript. Meetings the recorder attended but did NOT record are labeled "(not recorded — no transcript)" and must not be passed to the transcript tools; meetings still being recorded/processed are labeled "(recording in progress — transcript not ready yet)" and may have one later. Add where "status/latest/code" eq "READY" to see only recorded meetings.
- native_calendarevent = scheduled calendar entries, past AND future (a past entry proves only that a meeting was scheduled — what happened lives on native_meetingrecording; an empty calendar result over past days says NOTHING about whether meetings happened, so answer past-meeting questions from native_meetingrecording, not from calendar rows or their absence): use a tight timeframe + "attendees" contains <email> and/or "domains" contains <domain>. To learn WHO an already-found event is with, fetch that event by objectIds with propertiesToReturn ["attendees","organizerEmail"] — the attendee list ({email, name, status, isOrganizer}) names the counterpart directly; never guess among name-matched contacts when the event is in hand. Results may carry visibilityNotes describing whose meetings are missing (private sharing, no connected calendar) — relay that caveat and NEVER assert someone is free or has no meetings from an empty result. Rows whose organizer is a current or former member of this workspace carry organizerAccount {membership: active|deactivated, deactivatedAt, calendarSync, lastCalendarSyncAt, note} — a deactivated membership or dead sync means the organizer is no longer active in Day AI (treat their events as historical); it does NOT tell you whether they still work at their company, and a missing organizerAccount means only that the organizer is not a Day AI user here — unless the response carries organizerAccountNote (the lookup failed), in which case every organizer's status is unknown. To find meetings ABOUT something, "content" contains <a few topic words> relevance-ranks by BM25 over title/summary/notes/transcript with a quoted excerpt per hit (one content term with all the words, not an OR of single words). native_page: the same content term ranks page TITLES (bodies are not indexed; read_page for the body); "title" contains remains the exact, database-fresh filter for a page you know by name.
- native_draft = unsent drafts (agent- or user-created): by recipient via the "hasRecipient" relationship → native_contact (resolve the contact by email first, then use its objectId); "my drafts" via the "creator" relationship → native_user with YOUR OWN user id (it is in your context; creator search is self-only — filtering by other users is not supported); by "email/subject" contains, "status" eq DRAFT, or a timeframe for recent drafts. A draft created for you in another conversation is found the same way.
- native_thread = past chat threads you can access: a content term ("content"/"text"/"title" contains) searches what was said in them and returns up to 5 threads with quoted excerpts, never the current one. Add timeframeStart/End for "last week"; "objectReferences" contains <objectId> for threads that touched a resolved object. Escalate to get_thread_context to read one thread in depth.
- Notes/deal context (deal notes, buyer voice, status updates) saved on opportunities/organizations/people: search the parent object with includeRelationships true — each native_context relationship entry returns the note inline as noteTitle/noteText, with noteWrittenAt (when it was written) — a later meeting or email supersedes an older note. If an entry has truncated true, call read_page with its pageId for the full note. For opportunity notes check BOTH the opp AND its organization.

TIMEFRAMES: timeframeStart/End (ISO or YYYY-MM-DD); timeframeField is strictly createdAt|updatedAt|storedAt|time|writtenAt (omit for the per-type default: "time" for native_emailmessage, updatedAt otherwise; "time" is emails-only — object-specific fields like startTime are NOT valid here; "writtenAt" is the search index's last-write time for incremental sync ONLY — it is not a property and is not "recently changed", use updatedAt for that). PAGINATION: each page returns status (partial|complete) and returnedCount (partial pages also carry totalRecords + a directive paginationNote). totalRecords is exact unless totalRecordsIsLowerBound is true, in which case it is a FLOOR — the real total is at least that, possibly far more, so treat it as evidence to keep paging, never as evidence you are nearly done. status "partial" means the result is INCOMPLETE — do NOT answer, count, or summarize from it; call again with the SAME queries and TOP-LEVEL offset=nextOffset — offset is a call-level parameter, not a field of a queries[] entry (past 10,000 rows, set paginationMode "cursor" from the first call and pass back nextCursor), merging every page until status is "complete". For a specific detail across many heavy records (e.g. native_opportunity: "last activity for all closed-lost opps"), pass a FOCUSED propertiesToReturn — just the fields you need, NOT "*" — so each page stays dense and the full set returns in far fewer round trips; don't drop to surface-only fields and don't stop early.

EXAMPLE:
{"description":"Searching for your open tasks","queries":[{"objectType":"native_action","where":{"AND":[{"propertyId":"ownerEmail","operator":"eq","value":"me@day.ai"},{"propertyId":"status","operator":"neq","value":"COMPLETED"},{"propertyId":"status","operator":"neq","value":"DISMISSED"},{"propertyId":"status","operator":"neq","value":"REDUNDANT"}]}}]}

</details>

### resolve_dates

*read-only* — Deterministic date/time calculator.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requests` | object \\| object \\| object \\| object \\| object \\| object[] | yes | The date questions to resolve, up to 25 per call. |

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Deterministic date/time calculator. ALWAYS use this tool instead of mental arithmetic for ANY weekday, relative-date, or timezone question — "what day of the week is X", "next week", "later this week", "end of month", date/time ± N units (seconds through years), listing the dates in a range, or converting a time between zones. Model-computed date arithmetic is unreliable; this tool is exact.
Batch every date question of the turn into one call (up to 25 requests). Operations:
- now: current date and time in a timezone.
- weekday_of: the weekday of a YYYY-MM-DD date.
- add_subtract: a starting point plus/minus any unit from seconds through years (negative amount subtracts). Pass exactly one of date ("2026-08-13") or datetime ("2026-08-13 15:00", "2026-08-13T15:00:00Z"). A date with a day-or-larger unit is pure calendar math; a datetime or a time unit (seconds/minutes/hours) returns a zone-aware datetime.
- enumerate_span: every date between two dates inclusive, each with its weekday (max 400 days).
- convert_zone: an instant converted between IANA timezones.
- resolve_expression: a named relative expression — today, yesterday, tomorrow, next/last/this <weekday> (e.g. "next Friday"), this/next/last week, later this week, this/next/last month, quarter, or year, end of day/week/month/quarter/year, EOD/EOW/EOM/EOQ/EOY, end or early/mid/late of a named or relative month ("end of October", "mid September", "end of next month", "mid next week"), named months/quarters and explicit dates ("January 2027", "Q1 2027", "November 1", "2026-11-01"), first/last week of a month, business-day offsets ("in 3 business days", "2 business days ago"), and common Korean forms ("다음 주", "10월 초", "10월 1일", "올해 말", "3영업일 후") — resolved to an explicit span with stamped endpoints and weekday-labeled dates. Unrecognized expressions return a structured "unrecognized" result, never a guess. When the expression comes from a source event (a meeting transcript, an email), pass anchorIso with the source's typed date so it resolves against the day it was said, not today.
"next <weekday>" is that weekday of NEXT week and "last <weekday>" is that weekday of LAST week — never the current week's occurrence. When a nearer occurrence exists this week, the result includes an interpretationNote and the nearerAlternative date: relay that caveat to the user, and use "this <weekday>" for the current week's occurrence.
Week expressions are bounded per the weekMode parameter (see its description for the per-expression defaults).
Timezone defaults to the user's zone; pass an IANA timezone (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles") to override.

</details>

## Opportunities & pipeline

### create_or_update_opportunity

*writes · can overwrite* — Creates or updates a single Opportunity object, with optional batch support capped at 15 operations.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isCreating` | boolean |  | Explicitly control whether to create (true) or update (false) an opportunity. |
| `objectId` | string |  | For updates: provide the existing opportunity ID. |
| `standardProperties` | object |  | Standard properties as key-value pairs (e.g., { title: "Deal Name", stageId: "uuid" }). |
| `customProperties` | object[] |  | Custom properties to update. |
| `allowDuplicate` | boolean |  | Create even though the organization already has an open opportunity in this pipeline. |
| `dateProvenance` | object |  | REQUIRED whenever a date value in this call was extracted from a source object (a meeting, an email) rather than stated directly by the user in this conversati… |
| `operations` | object[] |  | Optional batch mode: array of opportunity create/update operations (1-15 items). |

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Creates or updates a single Opportunity object, with optional batch support capped at 15 operations. For bulk imports, prefer batch_create_or_update_opportunities. The server checks every create for an existing open opportunity on the same organization and blocks duplicates; a blocked create returns the existing objectId — update that instead of re-creating. Only pass allowDuplicate: true after the user confirms this is a separate deal. Searching first with search_objects (objectType="native_opportunity", relationship "subject" to targetObjectType "native_organization") is still the fastest way to find the record you should be updating, and it gives you the organizationId to pass on create. Always call read_crm_schema before creating or updating. Opportunities require a valid stageId. ownerEmail may be any valid email, including a historical owner who is no longer a workspace member; current workspace member emails also link the native user assignee. CRITICAL: Every opportunity must have either an organization (organizationId, or a business domain) OR at least one person attached via roles — prefer the organization whenever available. Opportunities without an organization or roles cannot auto-populate their custom properties.

</details>

### batch_create_or_update_opportunities

*writes · can overwrite* — Batch create or update multiple opportunities at once.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operations` | object[] | yes | Array of opportunity create/update operations (1-25 items) |

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Batch create or update multiple opportunities at once. The server checks every create for an existing open opportunity on the same organization and blocks duplicates (including a second row in the same batch that resolves to the same organization); a blocked create returns the existing objectId — update that instead of re-creating. Only pass allowDuplicate: true with acknowledgedDuplicateOf after the user confirms a separate deal. Searching first with search_objects (objectType="native_opportunity", relationship "subject" to targetObjectType "native_organization") is still the fastest way to find the records you should be updating, and it gives you the organizationId to pass on create. Always call read_crm_schema before creating or updating. CRITICAL: Every opportunity must have either an organization (organizationId, or a business domain) OR at least one person attached via roles — prefer the organization whenever available. Opportunities without an organization or roles cannot auto-populate their custom properties.

</details>

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Generate longer-form content in a separate page. If the user asked for a Google Doc, Word document, or another external document format: Day has no direct export to those formats — still create the Page, but tell the user this explicitly and offer the two real options: copy/paste the page into their editor (rich formatting like headings, bold, lists, links, and tables carries over), or make the page public and share the link. Pages support rich layout panels via <day-ai-panel variant="card|callout|fold" tone="neutral|info|warning|success" title="...">block content</day-ai-panel>: card for bordered summary/lead cards (optionally with a headline metric via metric="27%" and metric-caption="..."), callout for a tinted next-action or warning strip, fold for collapsed-by-default method/debug detail — plus horizontal progress meters via <day-ai-meter value="27" max="100" tone="accent|positive|warning|neutral"></day-ai-meter> and inline fact/status pills via <day-ai-chip label="First touch" tone="neutral|info|warning|success"></day-ai-chip>.

</details>

### get_campaign_details

*read-only* — Get campaign details including title, purpose, assignment instructions, sequencing config, send schedule, statuses, member count, and a read-back of the live drafting skill.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `campaignId` | string | yes | The UUID of the campaign to retrieve. |

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Get campaign details including title, purpose, assignment instructions, sequencing config, send schedule, statuses, member count, and a read-back of the live drafting skill. Use this before working campaign members to understand the campaign context and assignment rules. When describing when the campaign sends, use `sendScheduleSummary` verbatim — do not infer a schedule from any other field. When describing the campaign's daily send limit, use `dailySendLimit` (status `off`, `effective` with its `summary`, or `not_in_effect` — saved but NOT enforced; never call that limit active). You can set or clear the limit with create_or_update_campaign (`dailySendLimit`), but approving, sending, scheduling an email, or sending past a limit are done by the user in the campaign UI — direct them there. When asked what an email/touch N says or what its theme is, answer from `drafting.touchPlan` (the touch-by-touch section of the drafting skill the drafts actually run on) TOGETHER WITH `drafting.ownerRefinements` (the owner's standing rules, which also govern every touch — a rule about one touch can live there rather than on its touch line). Those two fields are the touch themes and the standing rules, not the whole skill: voice, grounding, and campaign sections also shape drafts, so for a full explanation of why drafts read a certain way, read the skill itself (manage_skills action "get" on `drafting.skillId`). Never answer any of this from the campaign's stored `messagingPlan` property (via search_objects or anywhere else): that is the setup-time plan, read once at provisioning, and it goes stale as soon as drafting is refined. If `drafting` is null, the live drafting instructions are unavailable: the campaign may not have a drafting skill yet, or the read may have failed. Do not claim that no skill exists or substitute the setup-time plan; retry the read before explaining current instructions.

</details>

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Visualize data as a FROZEN bar, line, area, composed, pie, scatter, radar, radial bar, treemap, funnel, sunburst, sankey, stat (single big-number tile with optional previous-period delta + sparkline), barList (ranked meter list), or heatmap (row × column intensity matrix) snapshot — or draw a decisionTree logic diagram (qualification flows, routing rules, playbooks) with labeled yes/no branches. Supports the same rendering extras as live widgets: footnote (muted methodology line under the plot), annotations + showValues on cartesian charts, and creation-time topN/Other rollup for high-cardinality categories (UUID-looking labels always fold into "Unknown"). The data is whatever you pass at call time — it will NEVER update. DO NOT use this for live CRM data, dashboards, or anything tied to a recurring query — use create_widget (live) or create_table_widget (live) instead. For anything embedded on a page or dashboard, use create_widget instead — a create_chart is a static snapshot and will not refresh. create_widget supports edge-property dimensions (campaign-member status, etc.) and KPI single-value widgets, so there is rarely a reason to fall back to a static create_chart for CRM-derived visualizations. Use create_chart ONLY for one-off snapshots of data you computed in code_execution that has no recurring source query — e.g. a derived breakdown you generated from a CSV. decisionTree is the exception to the create_widget guidance: it visualizes authored logic, not query data, so it always belongs here.

</details>

### create_widget

*read-only* — Create a live dashboard widget that queries, groups, and charts CRM data, recomputed on every page load.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | object | yes | What to query. |
| `groupBy` | object |  | Dimension to group rows by (the chart categories). |
| `breakdown` | object |  | Optional second dimension → one series per value. |
| `topN` | integer |  | Root-level: cap groupBy categories to the N largest by measure; the rest roll into one "Other" category (label via root "otherLabel", default "Other"). |
| `otherLabel` | string |  | Label for the rolled-up remainder produced by topN / breakdownTopN. |
| `breakdownTopN` | integer |  | Root-level: cap breakdown series / heatmap columns to the N largest by total measure; the rest roll into one "Other" series/column (label via root "otherLabel"… |
| `measure` | object |  | What to compute per group: - "count" (default). |
| `edgeProperties` | object[] |  | Pre-hydrate edge values onto rows as "<relationship>__<field>" for consumers other than a kind:"edge" dimension (ratio sub-filters, breakdowns, attribute dims)… |
| `relatedFilters` | object[] |  | Fixed cross-object filters for criteria on a related object (same shape as table widgets): { "targetType", "link": { "kind": "property", "baseProperty": "owner… |
| `filters` | object |  | Optional viewer-facing dropdowns above the chart (up to 3 independent; selection is local-only and refetches with it merged in): { "value"?: { "label", "field"… |
| `chart` | object | yes | How to render the result. |

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Create a live dashboard widget that queries, groups, and charts CRM data, recomputed on every page load. Must be added to a page to make a dashboard. The user cannot see the widget until it is on a page. Supports count/sum/avg/min/max, ratio (current-stage win/conversion rates), funnel measure (stage-history conversion between any two stage sets for opportunities), and weighted sums (Σ(field × weight) with the weight optionally joined from a related object — e.g. amount × stage.likelihoodToClose for forecasting). Group by attribute, foreign-key-resolved attribute (a "resolve" spec is REQUIRED when grouping/breaking down on stageId or pipelineId — raw ids are not valid labels), calendar datePart, relative date buckets (Overdue / This Month / Later), relationship, relationshipClassification (such as internal vs external attendee organizations), or EDGE property (values on the relationship itself, e.g. campaign-member status). Chart types: bar/line/area/pie/funnel/barList (one dimension), sankey/heatmap (two dimensions), OR "kpi"/"stat" for single-number widgets (omit groupBy). Prefer "stat" over "kpi" for headline metrics — it can carry a trailing trend sparkline (chart.spark) and a previous-period delta (chart.compare, needs a bounded timeframe). Use "barList" instead of bar for ranked category comparisons of ≤12 rows (readable labels, meter bars); barList rows can carry a secondary per-row marker metric (chart.marker, e.g. avg deal size per stage). Use "heatmap" for two-dimension intensity (groupBy rows × breakdown columns; cells with no data render empty, not zero). Cap high-cardinality dimensions with root topN (groupBy categories) and breakdownTopN (breakdown series / heatmap columns) — the remainder rolls into "Other". Cartesian charts support chart.annotations (category-anchored event callouts) and chart.showValues (print values on bars/points). Use chart.footnote for a muted one-line methodology/caveat footer under the plot instead of putting that in the description or in prose after the widget. Use relatedFilters for fixed cross-object filters and filters.relatedValue for viewer-facing cross-object dropdowns. Use edgeProperties to pre-hydrate edge values for ratio sub-filters and breakdowns that consume them outside of a kind:"edge" dimension. Pass `filters` to render per-widget viewer-facing dropdowns (value filter / timeframe / group-by / related-value) above the chart — the viewer picks an option and the widget refetches with the selection merged in (selection is local, not persisted). ALWAYS PREFER create_widget OVER create_chart for live CRM data — create_chart produces a frozen snapshot that does not update. Custom-property field UUIDs (measure.field/weightField, groupBy/breakdown, where) must be copied verbatim from read_crm_schema — a fabricated or typo'd UUID is rejected at create time.

</details>

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

A dashboard is charts-first: reach for create_widget before this tool; a flat record table is the appendix of a dashboard, never its body. Create a LIVE dashboard table widget, recomputed server-side on every load; embed it on a page for the user to see it. THREE MODES: flat list (omit grouping/aggregations), grouped list (grouping only), or PIVOT/SUMMARY (grouping + aggregations — one row per group with inline aggregates + grand total, no record rows). Use pivot whenever the user asks for "summary"/"rollup"/"pivot"/"key metrics"/"% of total"/"count per X". Aggregation ops: sum/avg/min/max, size, countDistinct, pctOfTotal; multiple aggregations on one field are idiomatic. The result includes "warnings" when an aggregation's field yields no value on the matched rows — heed them before embedding. Cross-object: relatedColumns surfaces fields from related objects (or from the EDGE itself, e.g. campaign-member status), relatedFilters narrows by a related object's property — both resolve live; never hardcode pre-resolved ids into source.where. Flat/grouped tables support per-column rich treatments via "columnFormats": meter bars for scores, heat cells for bounded ordinals (0-3 rubric points), toned badges for categorical statuses, and stacked identity cells (bold name over muted email) — declare them instead of dumping raw numbers. Use "footnote" for a muted one-line methodology/caveat note under the table instead of prose after the widget. Custom-property field UUIDs (columns, columnFormats, where) must be copied verbatim from read_crm_schema — a fabricated or typo'd UUID is rejected at create time.

</details>

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Export CRM data as a CSV file for a subsequent execute_code turn. Use this before execute_code when analyzing CRM data with Python. Prefer passing columns or view_id to avoid wide, slow exports. Do not call it from inside Python expecting immediate access in the current sandbox. Email exports include emailSyncContext for interpreting result freshness. Opportunity exports include enriched stage names, stage types, and pipeline names. Do not treat updatedAt as a proxy for deal progress or "not stalled"; use includeStageHistory for stalled/time-in-stage analysis. Set includeStageHistory: true only when the analysis requires time-in-stage, funnel conversion, or velocity metrics. Supports native_campaign and native_campaignmemberstatus exports. For "members of campaign X" exports, set objectType to native_contact, filter `where` to contacts whose memberOf relationship points to the campaign, and use `edgeProperties` to surface per-member fields (status, addedAt, owner, notesToSelf, sequenceState) which live on the relationship and would otherwise be invisible. Omit edgeProperties.targetObjectId for workspace-wide contact campaign-membership exports: one row per live edge, including memberOf__targetObjectId; contacts without memberships are omitted.

</details>

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Manage agent skills and workspace Skill Library items: list, get, create, update, delete, reset prompts, manage Page or Folder attachments, view edit history, or (Admins/Owners) deploy/undeploy library skills to teammates' agents. action=deploy assigns a library skillId to the agents in targetAssistantIds (Managed skills stay synced to the source; Template skills fork); action=undeploy removes it from the listed agents only (Template forks survive). Both are additive/subtractive per listed agent — nothing unlisted changes — and return per-agent statuses. Campaign skills are NOT created here: a campaign's drafting coordinator, status-update, and drafter skills (slash commands campaign-drafting-<id>, campaign-status-<id>, campaign-drafter-<id>) are provisioned automatically by Day AI when the campaign is sampled or launched (draft_campaign_outreach), onto the agent that works it. Never create, recreate, or hand-build skills for a campaign, even as a delegated task or by copying an existing campaign's skills as a template — a hand-built copy has no campaign lineage, does nothing, and blocks the real provisioning. If a user asks to "set up the campaign's skills", explain that Launch (or a sample) does this and offer to launch or sample the campaign instead; if a campaign skill is structurally broken (missing sections, corrupted prompt), repair its prompt with action=update rather than recreating it. Drafting refinements for a campaign — feedback on a campaign's drafts about voice, tone, signature/sign-off, length, content rules, things to never say — do NOT go through this tool: call refine_campaign_drafting instead (destination "email_writing" when the feedback is about how the sender writes in general), which targets the right drafter fork on the working agent and reconciles the instructions. A standing rule about how an agent writes that is NOT feedback on a campaign's drafts belongs in that agent's Email Writing skill, edited here (with targetAssistantId when it is another agent). action=update on a campaign drafter/coordinator skill is only for structural repair of a broken skill, never for changing how the campaign drafts. Confirm the target list with the user before deploying; read current holders first via action=get (assignedAssistantIds). Use action=get with skillId before describing a focused skill or changing its prompt/attachments; get returns attachment instructions and their scope. attachmentChanges is granular: upsert/detach only the requested Pages or Folders, or use clearAll=true. For prompt updates, prefer a targeted edit (oldPromptMatch + newPromptReplace) over the prompt field — prompt fully replaces the existing prompt and anything omitted is lost. Use action=list_versions (then get_version) to view previous saved versions of a skill's prompt or other fields — e.g. to recover a prompt that was accidentally overwritten — and restore one via action=update. Use action=list with targetScope="workspace_library" to find workspace Skill Library items. For normal agent-skill create, omit targetScope or set targetScope="agent"; use triggerType="SCHEDULE" with a 15-minute-aligned cron for daily, weekdays, weekly, or every-4-hours schedules, triggerType="EVENT" with triggerValue="SLACK_SUMMARY_READY", or triggerType="NEITHER" for no trigger. For workspace library create, set targetScope="workspace_library"; ask users for a Managed skill or Template skill, then encode Managed as deploymentMode="SHARED" and Template as deploymentMode="TEMPLATE" in the tool call. Managed skill create/update is workspace-admin only, and Template skill create is allowed for paid users. User-created agent skills may set mcpProviders on create or update (any trigger type, including none); each added connector must already be connected by the agent owner in User Settings → Connectors. In workspaces where the managed-connector fast pass is enabled, Managed workspace skills may set mcpProviders=["hubspot"] to use each agent owner's existing HubSpot connection without separate member approval; other Managed-skill connector additions, and Managed-skill connector writes outside enabled workspaces, are rejected. Workspace library field edits are allowed for workspace admins, and template field edits/deletes are also allowed for the template creator. Do not present SHARED or TEMPLATE as product labels in user-facing replies. Managed workspace skills cannot be deleted through chat; deletion is reserved for the manual Skills Library UI. Day AI library template definitions are code-defined, not editable workspace-library source records; create a workspace library copy for team customization. timezone is only valid for SCHEDULE triggers. If an automated-trigger update fails because no slots remain, explain that all automated slots are already used on the current tier and suggest disabling another automated skill trigger or upgrading. If create returns created=true with success=false, never retry create; update the returned skillId. action=reset_prompt restores defaults only. Never claim an action succeeded unless this tool returns success.

</details>

<details><summary>Full description</summary>

Manage the Day AI workspace's team: add (invite) a person by email, resend or revoke an invite, list members and their roles, change a member's or invitee's role (Owner, Admin, Member), remove a member, and configure auto-invite for claimed company domains. Adding someone sends an email invite they must accept; use invite_member with the roleId for the role they should get. Workflow: call list_configuration FIRST to get availableRoles (roleId values), current members, and your own permissions; then invite_member / update_member_role / update_invite_role / remove_member by email. remove_member is destructive and irreversible from this tool: confirm with the user before calling it.

</details>
